name: datasource
summary: The pluggable connector layer plus everything about a saved data source: encrypted credentials, the Google Sheets OAuth connection, schema introspection, and read-only query execution. The largest backend package and the one every report path reaches through.
exposes: Connector interface: TestConnection(ctx), Introspect(ctx) (Schema, error), QueryLanguage() string, RunQuery(ctx, query, args, limit) (QueryResult, error)
NewConnector(sourceType, ConnectionConfig) — factory over connectorRegistry; SupportedTypes = [postgres, mysql]
Resolver.Resolve(ctx, userID, dataSourceID) (DataSource, Connector, error) — the one way to get a live connector for a saved source
Schema{Tables []Table, Fields []string} and Schema.Describe() string (LLM-facing text form)
Store CRUD (Create, CreateSheetsSource, List, Get, Delete), SchemaStore, SheetsStore
HTTP: GET/POST /api/datasources, POST /api/datasources/test, DELETE /api/datasources/{id}, GET /api/datasources/{id}/schema, POST /api/datasources/{id}/schema/refresh, the four google-sheets routes
key_notes: google_sheets is deliberately NOT in connectorRegistry: its connector is built from an OAuth token rather than a ConnectionConfig, so Resolver.connectorFor special-cases sheetsSourceType. Adding another OAuth-shaped source means touching that function.

One data_sources table holds both shapes. SQL columns (host/port/db_name/username/encrypted_password) and Sheets columns (spreadsheet_id/spreadsheet_name/google_connection_id) are all nullable, and DataSource uses *string/*int for them. migration 0004 dropped the NOT NULLs.

Schema is read once at connect time and stored in data_source_schemas (JSONB, one row per source). Query building never touches the user's DB — a stale schema is the usual cause of 'X is not a table/column, refresh its schema' errors. Users fix it via POST .../schema/refresh.
storeSchema() in handlers.go is best-effort: if introspection fails at connect time the source is still saved and the failure is only logged. SchemaProvider.Schema then lazily retries on first read.

SQL RunQuery opens a READ ONLY transaction as a second line of defence; the compiled query text comes from internal/query and is never client-supplied. Both SQL connectors open a fresh connection per call — no pooling of user databases.

The Sheets connector reads only the FIRST sheet of a spreadsheet, and its 'schema' is the header row (Schema.Fields). Queries go to the gviz endpoint (docs.google.com/.../gviz/tq), which returns JSONP that unwrapGviz strips. That endpoint has NO parameter binding, so RunQuery errors if args are non-empty — internal/query/sheets.go inlines literals instead.

Sheets OAuth is a separate flow from sign-in with its own scopes (spreadsheets.readonly + drive.metadata.readonly), its own cookies (sheets_oauth_state, sheets_oauth_user), and requires a refresh token — it uses AccessTypeOffline + ApprovalForce and rejects a grant without one.
GET /api/datasources/google-sheets/login takes the JWT as a ?token= query param, because it is reached by a plain browser navigation that cannot set an Authorization header.
postgres DSN uses sslmode=prefer; MySQL DSN uses timeout=5s. Credentials are URL-escaped in the Postgres DSN but NOT in the MySQL one.
normalizeValue (query.go) converts driver []byte to string and time.Time to RFC3339 so results survive JSON encoding — everything downstream assumes that normalization happened.
